summary: Port CBL0008 (account report) to a Python module that reproduces its report from the sample ACCTREC file and adds a one-byte OVER-LIMIT flag at byte 65 of each detail line, preceded by two spaces at bytes 63-64. All print lines become 65 bytes. OVER-LIMIT is 'Y' when ACCT-BALANCE is greater than ACCT-LIMIT and 'N' otherwise, with no printed heading. The run date is masked only in test comparisons.

new_fields.name: OVER-LIMIT
new_fields.purpose: One-byte flag at byte 65 of each detail line, after two spaces at bytes 63-64. 'Y' when ACCT-BALANCE is greater than ACCT-LIMIT, otherwise 'N' (equal is 'N'). No printed heading.

acceptance_criteria: On the sample ACCTREC file, the Python TLIMIT total equals the sum of ACCT-LIMIT over all records read and equals the TLIMIT value CBL0008 prints.
On the sample ACCTREC file, the Python TBALANCE total equals the sum of ACCT-BALANCE over all records read and equals the TBALANCE value CBL0008 prints.
For a record with ACCT-BALANCE greater than ACCT-LIMIT, OVER-LIMIT is 'Y'.
For one synthetic test record with ACCT-BALANCE equal to ACCT-LIMIT, OVER-LIMIT is 'N'. The synthetic record is used in tests only and is never added to the sample file.
For a record with ACCT-BALANCE less than ACCT-LIMIT, OVER-LIMIT is 'N'.
Each detail line is 65 bytes long: bytes 63-64 are spaces and byte 65 is OVER-LIMIT ('Y' or 'N').
Every print line (header, detail and totals) is 65 bytes long, padded with spaces on the right.
No heading is printed for OVER-LIMIT, and the text of HEADER-1 to HEADER-4 is unchanged.
Byte positions refer to the logical print record, and the Python output writes no ASA carriage-control byte.

Apart from bytes 63-65 of each detail line, the padding to 65 bytes and the run-date characters masked in the test comparison, the Python report equals the CBL0008 output byte for byte on the sample file.
The run date is masked only in test comparisons; the Python module does not mask it in its output.
analysis_notes: From CBL0008.cobol, confirm that PRINT-REC is the 62-byte report record (ACCT-NO-O, FILLER X(02), LAST-NAME-O, FILLER X(02), ACCT-LIMIT-O, FILLER X(02), ACCT-BALANCE-O, trailing FILLER X(02)) and that no item lies beyond byte 62, so that the new bytes 63-65 are added at the end of the record.

From CBL0008.cobol, identify the WORKING-STORAGE items TLIMIT and TBALANCE (not in data-dictionary.md, so they are not in fields[]), their PIC and USAGE, and the paragraph that accumulates them over every record read.

From CBL0008.cobol, identify the edited items TLIMIT-O and TBALANCE-O that print the totals, their PIC and byte positions, and the length of the totals line before it is moved into PRINT-REC. Confirm the spelling of these names as in CBL0008.cobol.
From CBL0008.cobol, check whether the MOVE of TLIMIT and TBALANCE into the edited totals items can drop high-order digits, since the edited pictures may hold fewer integer digits than the totals.
From CBL0008.cobol, identify which of HEADER-1 to HEADER-4 contain characters written from WS-CURRENT-DATE-DATA, with their byte positions, so that the test comparison masks exactly those bytes.
From CBL0008.cobol, confirm the WRITE PRINT-REC statements and the record area they use, so that the Python output matches the logical print record excluding any ASA carriage-control byte.

From the sample ACCTREC file named in the ticket, confirm the record length (170 bytes per the ACCT-FIELDS layout that CBL0008 reads) and the record count, and list the record numbers with ACCT-BALANCE below and above ACCT-LIMIT for the OVER-LIMIT tests. The expected TLIMIT and TBALANCE values may be derived from the file, per ticket comment 10007.
